# Clause– Antagonism And Roleplay Antagonists are expected to roleplay, and like Security and Command are held to [textlink="higher standards" link="ClauseSpL1"]. You are likely to be the main driver of conflict in a given round– the ball is entirely in your court.
You have free reign to [textlink="ambush" link="ClauseSpL2"] kill and steal targets, but should still consider your footprint. 9 times out of 10, you will be required to escape to CentComm alive and unrestrained, and should avoid going too loud as a result.
You should avoid intentionally targeting individuals unrelated to your objectives where possible, and you should never find yourself mowing down civilians unless you have explicit admin approval to do so.
## Customizing Objectives Antagonists may AHelp to request modifications to their objectives. This can range from simply removing a kill objective to, provided an admin is onboard with helping, a full custom mission to complete over the course of the shift. Alternatively, antagonists may entirely disregard their objectives with admin permission, granted that they find other means of causing disruption and making the round interesting.
The ability to customize your objectives is based on your behavior. If you are a consistently problematic antagonist or if multiple complaints have been levied against your conduct, you may be barred from requesting modifications, and non-disruptive objectives may be forced upon you. This may be escalated to a blanket antagonist ban if especially egregious.
## Free Agents Antagonists classified as free agents (wizards, changelings, vampires, and thieves) have no obligation to be conflict drivers, and should instead focus on their objectives.
In the case of changelings and vampires in particular, your priority should be surviving and avoiding discovery above all else.
